clinical_scope.population: Adults and young people aged 16 years or older unless otherwise specified by local protocol
excluded_populations: pediatric specialty pathways unless explicitly validated
clinical_scope.intended_use: High-risk candidate retrieval and guideline-based verification for suspected Encephalitis.
clinical_scope.important_boundary: This graph supports clinical reasoning and missed-diagnosis risk reduction; it is not an autonomous diagnostic system.

relationship_to_other_graphs.boundary_note: This graph focuses on suspected infectious encephalitis; autoimmune, paraneoplastic, toxic-metabolic, and vascular mimics must remain active differentials.

basic_info.working_definition: Encephalitis is inflammation of the brain parenchyma, usually presenting as encephalopathy plus evidence of CNS inflammation; infectious causes such as HSV are time-critical.
why_high_risk_for_missed_diagnosis: Can present as psychiatric change, delirium, seizure, fever, or focal deficit and be mistaken for stroke, intoxication, psychosis, migraine, or metabolic disease.
CSF may be initially nonspecific and early imaging may be normal.
HSV encephalitis requires early empiric acyclovir consideration because delays worsen outcomes.
Meningitis and encephalitis overlap, and both may require urgent empiric treatment.
basic_info.time_sensitivity: Suspected encephalitis with altered mental status, seizures, or focal deficits requires urgent neuroinfectious workup and empiric antiviral consideration.
do_not_use_as: a replacement for neurologist/infectious disease review

activation_logic.minimum_activation: Altered mental status/encephalopathy plus fever, seizure, focal deficit, CSF abnormality, MRI/EEG abnormality, or CNS infection risk.

strong_activation_patterns.reason: Encephalitis and HSV must be considered.

case_features: temporal lobe MRI or focal temporal EEG

weak_activation_patterns.reason: Fever alone does not suggest encephalitis.

symptom_to_candidate_retrieval.scoring_warning: Weights are for retrieval and explanation only. They are not calibrated probabilities and must not be used as a diagnostic score.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is there altered mental status, behavior change, reduced consciousness, or cognitive dysfunction?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Encephalitis less likely without encephalopathy, but focal CNS infection may remain possible.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are fever, CSF pleocytosis, MRI/EEG abnormalities, seizures, or focal deficits present?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If absent, evaluate mimics and autoimmune/metabolic causes.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is lumbar puncture safe and are CSF tests available?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Use CSF to support etiology; continue therapy if high suspicion.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Normal/early CSF does not always exclude encephalitis.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is HSV encephalitis possible and has HSV PCR/empiric acyclovir pathway been considered?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If HSV unlikely, consider other infectious/autoimmune etiologies.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: HSV status missing; do not falsely reassure.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Is MRI brain or CT available to evaluate inflammation, hemorrhage, stroke, mass, or abscess?
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: If normal early, encephalitis may still be possible.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Are seizures, nonconvulsive status epilepticus, or EEG abnormalities possible?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Manage seizures and support encephalitis verification.
guideline_verification_pathway.if_missing: EEG unavailable when persistent AMS or seizures suspected.

guideline_verification_pathway.check: Could meningitis, stroke, hemorrhage, toxic-metabolic encephalopathy, autoimmune encephalitis, or psychiatric illness explain the case?
guideline_verification_pathway.positive_result: Report competing diagnoses and parallel pathways.
guideline_verification_pathway.negative_result: Encephalitis remains if CNS inflammation evidence is present.

distinguishing_features: Meningeal symptoms predominate; altered mental status suggests meningoencephalitis overlap.
Acute focal deficit; fever/encephalopathy/seizures may be absent in pure stroke.
Sudden headache, vomiting, reduced consciousness, focal deficit.
Postictal confusion can mimic encephalitis; persistent AMS or fever/CSF/MRI abnormalities increase encephalitis concern.
Subacute psychiatric/cognitive symptoms, seizures, movement disorder, autonomic features; may lack fever.
Medication/toxin, electrolyte, hepatic, renal, hypoxic, or endocrine causes.

final_assessment.safety_statement: Clinical decision support only; urgent clinician assessment is required when a high-risk condition is suspected.

evidence_sources.title: IDSA Clinical Practice Guidelines: The Management of Encephalitis
key_points: Provides diagnostic and treatment guidance for suspected encephalitis and multiple infectious etiologies.
Used here for encephalopathy-plus-inflammation recognition, CSF testing, neuroimaging, EEG, PCR testing, and empiric acyclovir consideration.

evidence_sources.title: NICE NG240: Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management
evidence_sources.publisher: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
key_points: Covers recognition, diagnosis, and management of bacterial meningitis and meningococcal disease in babies, children, young people, and adults.
Used here for adult recognition, emergency treatment timing, lumbar puncture considerations, and meningococcal disease red flags.

must_not: Do not make an autonomous definitive diagnosis.
Do not use a single symptom, sign, laboratory result, score, or imaging clue as a standalone rule-in or rule-out criterion.
Do not provide patient-facing reassurance when critical red-flag data are missing.
Do not ignore competing high-risk differential diagnoses.
Do not replace local emergency, specialty, or hospital protocols.
Do not generate medication orders; recommend clinician-led pathway activation instead.
Do not exclude HSV encephalitis because early CT is normal.
Do not dismiss psychiatric symptoms without neurologic/infectious red-flag assessment.
Do not delay urgent empiric antiviral consideration in high-risk suspected HSV encephalitis.
must_do: Use this graph for candidate retrieval, missed-diagnosis risk reduction, and guideline-based verification.
Separate supporting evidence, evidence against, and missing critical information.
State whether verification is complete, partial, impossible from available data, or contradicted.
Include differential diagnoses that can mimic the condition.
Trace guideline-dependent claims to evidence IDs.
Mark output as clinical decision support requiring qualified clinician review.
Always determine whether encephalopathy is present.
Always evaluate seizure/status epilepticus and LP safety.
